readme.about: The README's generated blocks (pii-guard eval report rewrites the text between <!-- intro:start --> and <!-- intro:end -->, and between <!-- results:start --> and <!-- results:end -->). Layout 'compact' (LAB-1663): one table with a row per fixture set (columns) and a column per system (rows), each cell 'leak · over-masking', read from each set's latest snapshot in eval/results/runs/. Prose is editorial and lives here; numbers enter it only through placeholders filled from the records: {leak:<set>:<system>}, {over:...}, {partial:...}, {docs:<set>}, {langs:<set>}, {codes:<set>}, {ner_p50:<model in model_latency>}, {ner_p95:<model>}, {overhead_p50:<latency run id>} (one client, not streaming); a system is a run-record key or an alias. model_latency names the one model-latency measurement the README quotes (LAB-1625's gateway-latency records were taken under heavy load and are too noisy to quote).

model_latency.label: NER model time per message on CPU (the model alone, not the whole gateway)

bullets: **What it does.** An OpenAI-compatible gateway for AI agents. Change one base URL, and the names, addresses, IDs and faces it detects become reversible placeholders (`[[PERSON_7f3a]]`) before the request leaves. The real values come back in the answer, mid-stream and inside tool calls. Detection is rules plus a small NER that runs on CPU: XLM-RoBERTa base, distilled from Meta's Muse Glimmer 30B.

**How well.** On {docs:agent-traffic} fictional agent-traffic documents ({codes:agent-traffic}), {leak:agent-traffic:own} of personal values reached the model and {over:agent-traffic:own} of masks hit text that was not personal data. The lowest-leak alternative, PrivAiTe, leaked {leak:agent-traffic:privaite} and over-masked {over:agent-traffic:privaite} on the same documents.

**How fast.** The NER takes {ner_p50:v42-b3} per message on a laptop CPU (p50; p95 {ner_p95:v42-b3}, [measurement](eval/results/2026-10-30-lab-1625-ner-v42/latency-cpu-local.json)). No LLM call and no API cost in fast mode.

**Where your data goes.** In fast mode, the default (rules plus the on-device NER, no LLM call), the original text is processed only on your machine. The hosted demo receives what you type, so use fictional data there. The optional audit and SAM 3.1 endpoints receive the original text or pixels. Anything the detectors miss passes through: pseudonymization, not anonymization or a compliance guarantee.

notes: Leak: labeled personal values left fully readable in what the model receives. A value with only part left readable (a surname, the tail of a number) is a partial leak, counted separately: PII Guard fast {partial:agent-traffic:own} on agent traffic, {partial:smoke:own} on the hand-written set. Over-masking: masks on text that was not personal data. Lower is better for both; in each row, the lowest leak and the lowest over-masking are bold.
caveats: The sets are small (tens to hundreds of documents per language): a point or two of difference is noise. Agent traffic is written by Muse models from fictional seeds, which can flatter a detector taught by Muse labels; that is why the hand-written and public sets sit next to it.

Finance text is the weak spot. On Gretel finance's own labels PII Guard leaks {leak:gretel-finance:own}, about level with Presidio's {leak:gretel-finance:presidio}; on corrected labels ([why](docs/datasets.md)) {leak:gretel-finance-corrected:own} against {leak:gretel-finance-corrected:presidio}. Over-masking is high on Gretel finance ({over:gretel-finance:own}) and CEE-PII ({over:cee-pii:own}), where reference numbers without a cue word come out as IDs.

NER v4.2 leaks more than the previous v2.0 on CEE-PII ({leak:cee-pii:own} against {leak:cee-pii:v20}), the Polish pl-pii-bench ({leak:pl-pii-bench:own} against {leak:pl-pii-bench:v20}) and TAB court text ({leak:tab-echr:own} against {leak:tab-echr:v20}, scored locally only), and less on the hand-written sets, agent traffic and the EU multilingual set ([model notes](docs/models.md)).

lines: Every tool ran on the same documents (byte-identical files) and was scored by the same code; comparison tools use their documented defaults ([configurations](eval/results/2026-10-27-comparison/README.md#systems)). All data is fictional. PII Guard fast is rules plus the published NER `v4.2` ([model card](training/ner/model-card.md)). The hand-written set pools {codes:smoke}; the full tables, per-language numbers, Ai4Privacy (in-distribution for the NER, so not a win) and the corrected finance labels are in the [benchmark report](docs/benchmarks.md#results-by-fixture-set).
